subject: New paper on Distance software: Published

messages.author: 5900eadecec2d82d
messages.subject: New paper on Distance software: Published
parts:
Dear Distance software users,

Further to my message of 20th November (copied below), our paper on
Distance has now been published, and is now the default citation for the
software. The citation is:

Thomas, L., S.T. Buckland, E.A. Rexstad, J.L. Laake, S. Strindberg, S.L.
Hedley, J.R.B. Bishop, T.A. Marques and K.P. Burnham. 2010. Distance
software: design and analysis of distance sampling surveys for
estimating population size. Journal of Applied Ecology 47:5-14.

The paper is freely available to everyone under an OnlineOpen agreement
with the publisher, and copies can be downloaded from the publisher at
http://www3.interscience.wiley.com/journal/122685866/abstract
or
http://dx.doi.org/10.1111/j.1365-2664.2009.01737.x
or from our local university repository at
https://research-repository.st-andrews.ac.uk/handle/10023/817

If you have any problems obtaining a copy, please email me.

We suggest in your write-ups you continue to be explicit about the
version and release number of Distance you used, since results may vary
between versions. For example, you might write in a methods section:
"Analyses were carried out using Distance 6.0 release 2 (Thomas et al.
2010)"

We will update the "Citation" page of the Distance manual with the next
release.

Best wishes to all,

- Len Thomas

On 20/11/2009 12:40, Distance Development wrote:
> > Dear Distance users,
> >
> > We have written a paper describing the current capabilities of the
> > software and giving some hints on its use. Our goal in doing this was:
> > (1) to provide some useful information about the software
> > (2) to provide a standard peer-reviewed publication that users can cite
> > when referring to the software in their work
> >
> > The paper has been published online today in the Journal of Applied
> > Ecology. It will hopefully be in print early next year. We have arranged
> > for the electronic version to be freely available online. We hope to
> > host a copy locally in the future, but at present copies can be obtained
> > from:
> > http://www3.interscience.wiley.com/journal/122685866/abstract
> > or (direct link to pdf):
> > http://www3.interscience.wiley.com/cgi-bin/fulltext/122685866/PDFSTART
> >
> > The citation is:
> > Thomas, L., S.T. Buckland, E.A. Rexstad, J. L. Laake, S. Strindberg, S.
> > L. Hedley, J. R.B. Bishop, T. A. Marques, and K. P. Burnham. In press.
> > Distance software: design and analysis of distance sampling surveys for
> > estimating population size. Journal of Applied Ecology. DOI:
> > 10.1111/j.1365-2664.2009.01737.x
> >
> > This paper should now be treated as the standard citation for the
> > software. We will update the citation once it is in print (but the DOI
> > is an unique, permanent identifier), and also update our suggested
> > citation in the help pages of the Distance software with the next release.
> >
> > We suggest in your write-ups you continue to be explicit about the
> > version and release number of Distance you used, since results may vary
> > between versions. For example, you might write in a methods section:
> > "Analyses were carried out using Distance 6.0 release 2 (Thomas et al.
> > in press)"
> >
> > Wishing you all the best in your distance sampling survey work,
> >
> > - Len Thomas
> >

--
Len Thomas, Co-ordinator, Distance Development Project
Research Unit for Wildlife Population Assessment
Centre for Research into Environmental and Ecological Modelling
The Observatory, University of St Andrews, Scotland KY16 9LZ
